newsitem.title: USA: Billions more in air safety spending sought - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Billions more in air safety spending sought - WSJ.

text.p: A White House commission wants billions of dollars more to be spent to enhance aviation security and speed the improvement of the nation's air-traffic control system, the Wall Street Journal said Monday.

The latest proposals, scheduled to be announced Wednesday, call for at least $500 million in extra federal funding over the next five years to pay for high-priority airport-security projects, the paper said.
The report said the proposals do not back mandatory matching of checked baggage with passengers, which the airline industry had opposed as too costly and time-consuming.

Other parts of the commission's draft report recommend speeding up the deadline for relying on a satellite-based air-traffic-control system by five years earlier than planned, to the year 2005, the paper said.
